pinyin: zhì zhě qiān lǜ, bì yǒu yī shī
literal: wise man · thousand · considerations · surely · has · one · slip
natural: even the wise, after a thousand thoughts, will slip once

meaning.en: Even a very clever person will make a mistake sometimes.
meaning.zh: 再聪明的人，考虑多了也难免有疏漏。

equivalents: the best of us can slip up

examples.zh: 智者千虑，必有一失，这次的疏忽谁也不必苛责。
examples.en: Even the wisest slip up sometimes, so nobody should blame anyone for this oversight.

examples.zh: 他算无遗策，可惜必有一失，漏掉了最后一道审批。
examples.en: He planned everything, but even the best slip up and he missed the final approval.

examples.zh: 别太自责，智者千虑，必有一失。
examples.en: Don't blame yourself too much; even the wise make mistakes.

story.en: Li Zuoche tells Han Xin: 'The wise, with a thousand thoughts, will surely have one slip; the foolish, with a thousand thoughts, will surely have one gain' (智者千虑，必有一失；愚者千虑，必有一得).
story.zh: 广武君李左车对韩信说：“臣闻智者千虑，必有一失；愚者千虑，必有一得。”

usage.en: Used to console or to explain an oversight. The short form 必有一失 is common. Its pair: 愚者千虑，必有一得 ('even a fool has a good idea once').
usage.zh: 常用来安慰或解释疏漏。可省作“必有一失”。对句：“愚者千虑，必有一得”。

literal: look back · glance · self · a hero
natural: look around and think oneself a hero

meaning.en: To look around with pride, regarding oneself as a hero.
meaning.zh: 左顾右盼，自以为了不起，形容骄傲自负的样子。

examples.zh: 刚得了一点成绩，他就顾盼自雄，不可一世。
examples.en: With just a little success he already swaggers about, thinking himself a hero.

examples.zh: 他站在台上顾盼自雄，一副志得意满的样子。
examples.en: He stood on the stage looking around with an air of self-importance.

usage.en: Derogatory; describes arrogance in demeanour. Note: the 'hero' in 雄 is used as a verb ('to regard oneself as a hero').
usage.zh: 贬义；“雄”作动词，意为“自以为英雄”。

natural: sing of the wind and play with the moon

meaning.en: To write poems about natural scenery; also used for empty, sentimental writing.
meaning.zh: 吟咏风月，指写作诗文抒发闲情，有时也指内容空洞的文辞。

examples.zh: 他年轻时只会吟风弄月，不关心世事。
examples.en: In his youth he only composed poetry on wind and moon and cared nothing for world affairs.

examples.zh: 退休后他常在湖边吟风弄月，悠然自得。
examples.en: After retirement he often recites poems on moon and wind by the lake, perfectly content.

usage.en: Literary; can be mild praise (elegant leisure) or mild criticism (superficial or escapist writing). Often 吟风咏月.
usage.zh: 书面语，可雅可贬：雅指闲适，贬指内容空洞。

natural: a lump of elm wood

meaning.en: A dull and stubborn person who will not change his mind.
meaning.zh: 榆木质地坚硬、难以劈开；比喻头脑迟钝、固执不开窍的人。

examples.zh: 你真是个榆木疙瘩，怎么说都不开窍。
examples.en: You're a real blockhead; nothing I say gets through.

examples.zh: 他脑子就像榆木疙瘩，一点也不知道变通。
examples.en: His head is like a lump of elm; he has no flexibility at all.

usage.en: Colloquial insult or teasing. Often 榆木脑袋 or 榆木疙瘩脑袋. The 瘩 is neutral tone: gē da.
usage.zh: 口语，带嘲讽或打趣。也说“榆木脑袋”。“瘩”轻声。

natural: a future ten thousand li long

meaning.en: Used to wish someone a long and bright future; a promising career ahead.
meaning.zh: 前途远大、光明，常用作祝福语。

examples.zh: 祝你前程万里，一路顺风！
examples.en: I wish you a bright future and smooth sailing!

examples.zh: 这位年轻的科学家前程万里。
examples.en: This young scientist has a bright future ahead.

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长祝同学们前程万里。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the headmaster wished the students a bright future.

usage.en: Usually a farewell or graduation wish. Also 前程似锦, 鹏程万里 with the same meaning. 万里 is figurative.
usage.zh: 多用于送别、毕业祝福。也说“前程似锦、鹏程万里”。

natural: Wu's ribbons flutter in the wind

meaning.en: Praises painting in which the figures' robes and ribbons seem to flutter in the wind, in the manner of Tang painter Wu Daozi.
meaning.zh: 形容唐代画家吴道子所画人物衣带飘举、如迎风飘动的笔法；泛指人物画生动飘逸。

equivalents: figures that seem to flutter in the wind
fluid lines that capture the breeze

examples.zh: 他临摹的人物画吴带当风，线条流畅飘逸。
examples.en: His copies of figure paintings capture the wind-blown ribbons, with flowing lines.

examples.zh: 敦煌壁画的飞天，吴带当风，仿佛要飞出墙壁。
examples.en: The flying apsaras of the Dunhuang murals seem blown by the wind, as if about to fly off the wall.

usage.en: Art criticism; usually paired with 曹衣出水 (Cao Zhongda's 'clinging wet robes'). Used for traditional Chinese painting and sculpture.
usage.zh: 美术评论用语，常与“曹衣出水”并提，用于传统绘画、雕塑。

natural: heart and mouth agree

meaning.en: What one says matches what one thinks; honest and sincere.
meaning.zh: 心里想的和嘴上说的一致，坦诚直率。

examples.zh: 他为人心口如一，从不阳奉阴违。
examples.en: He is honest and straight-talking, and never pays lip service.

examples.zh: 做人要心口如一，说到做到。
examples.en: One should say what one means and do what one says.

usage.en: A compliment on honesty. Opposite 心口不一 / 口是心非.
usage.zh: 褒义，指为人诚实。反义词有“心口不一、口是心非”。

natural: fly ahead and surge forward

meaning.en: To make rapid, remarkable progress.
meaning.zh: 形容进步或发展极其迅速。

examples.zh: 经过一年苦练，她的英语水平突飞猛进。
examples.en: After a year of hard practice, her English has improved by leaps and bounds.

examples.zh: 近年来电动汽车技术突飞猛进。
examples.en: Electric vehicle technology has advanced rapidly in recent years.

examples.zh: 孩子的成绩突飞猛进，全家人都很高兴。
examples.en: The child's grades shot up and the whole family was delighted.

usage.en: Common in news and school contexts. Usually follows nouns like 技术、成绩、水平. Predicate.
usage.zh: 新闻、学习场景常用，多说“技术、成绩、水平突飞猛进”。

natural: blame cannot be escaped

meaning.en: Unable to escape punishment or blame for a crime or wrongdoing.
meaning.zh: 犯罪、过失的责任无法逃避。

examples.zh: 他在这起事故中罪责难逃。
examples.en: He cannot escape blame for this accident.

examples.zh: 证据确凿，被告罪责难逃。
examples.en: The evidence is conclusive and the defendant cannot escape guilt.

usage.en: Formal, common in news and legal contexts. Predicate.
usage.zh: 正式，多见于新闻和法律语境，作谓语。

natural: five sons pass the imperial exams

meaning.en: A traditional blessing for a family whose five sons all succeed in the imperial exams; today, a wish for many successes (a home, a car, savings, etc.).
meaning.zh: 五个儿子都科举及第；旧时用作祝福。今天也戏指在房子、车子等方面都有所成就。

examples.zh: 春节对联上写着“五子登科”，寓意子孙兴旺。
examples.en: The Spring Festival couplet says 'Five sons pass the exams', wishing a family of flourishing children.

examples.zh: 老一辈人总盼着五子登科。
examples.en: The older generation always hoped for five sons to pass the exams.

examples.zh: 这个新年愿望是“房子车子票子位子孩子”，号称现代版五子登科。
examples.en: This new year's wish is a house, a car, money, a post and a child: the modern 'five sons pass the exams'.

story.en: The Three Character Classic recalls Dou Yanshan of the Five Dynasties, who educated his five sons well: 'Dou Yanshan had the right method; he taught five sons, all famous' (窦燕山，有义方，教五子，名俱扬).
story.zh: 《三字经》：“窦燕山，有义方，教五子，名俱扬。”后人称其五子相继及第为“五子登科”。

usage.en: A festive blessing with traditional overtones; the modern joke version lists five 'zi' items. Often seen in decorative cards.
usage.zh: 带传统喜庆色彩的祝福语；现代戏谑版指“房子、车子、票子、位子、孩子”五个“子”。

literal: country · about to · not · be a country
natural: the nation is no longer a nation

meaning.en: The nation is in such chaos that it can hardly be called a country.
meaning.zh: 国家已经衰败到不成为国家的地步。

equivalents: the country is on the brink of collapse

examples.zh: 战乱不断，民不聊生，国将不国。
examples.en: With constant war and the people suffering, the country is hardly a country.

examples.zh: 政府如果失去民心，就会国将不国。
examples.en: If a government loses the people's trust, the nation will fall apart.

usage.en: Serious tone; often a warning. Also used rhetorically in political commentary. 国将不国 follows the pattern 'X将不X'.
usage.zh: 语气沉重，常用作警告，多见于政论。

natural: enmity against the nation and hatred against the family

meaning.en: Both national humiliation and personal family sufferings, combined into one bitter hatred.
meaning.zh: 国家遭受的屈辱和个人家庭遭受的仇恨；也指两者交织的深仇大恨。

equivalents: a nation's and a family's wrongs

examples.zh: 他把国仇家恨埋在心底，立志报效国家。
examples.en: He buried his anger against the enemy deep in his heart, and resolved to serve his country.

examples.zh: 小说主人公怀着国仇家恨走上战场。
examples.en: The novel's hero goes to battle with national and personal hatred.

usage.en: Usually appears in war stories and patriotic narratives. Also 家仇国恨 or 国恨家仇. Commonly combined with 血债.
usage.zh: 常见于战争、爱国题材。也说“家仇国恨、国恨家仇”。

natural: a nodding acquaintance

meaning.en: A casual acquaintance one just nods to when meeting.
meaning.zh: 仅仅认识，见面只点点头打招呼的一般交情。

examples.zh: 我跟他只是点头之交，谈不上了解。
examples.en: I'm only on nodding terms with him and hardly know him.

examples.zh: 网上的朋友大多只是点头之交。
examples.en: Most online friends are no more than nodding acquaintances.

usage.en: Neutral; often used when distancing oneself from someone. Contrasts with 莫逆之交 (bosom friend).
usage.zh: 中性，常用于撇清关系。与“莫逆之交”相对。

natural: treat with a cold eye

meaning.en: To treat someone with coldness and contempt.
meaning.zh: 用冷淡或轻视的态度对待别人。

examples.zh: 他落魄时，昔日的朋友都对他冷眼相待。
examples.en: When he fell on hard times, former friends gave him the cold shoulder.

examples.zh: 初来乍到，难免会遇到冷眼相待。
examples.en: When you are new, it's hard to avoid meeting a cold reception.

usage.en: Often used of social snubs; slightly literary. Note 冷眼旁观 is different: 'watch from the sidelines coolly'.
usage.zh: 多指受到冷落、轻视。注意与“冷眼旁观”（冷静地在旁观看）不同。

natural: nine times nine return to one

meaning.en: After all the complications, everything comes back to one point or ends at the same result.
meaning.zh: 经过种种曲折，最后归结到一个根本点上。

equivalents: it all comes down to one thing
everything returns to the starting point

examples.zh: 说来说去，九九归一，还是要靠自己努力。
examples.en: In the end it all comes down to the same point: you have to work hard yourself.

examples.zh: 几经周折，事情九九归一，回到原点。
examples.en: After many turns the matter came back to square one.

usage.en: Originally from arithmetic and folk calendar 'nine nines' of winter. Used in discussions and summaries as a concluding phrase.
usage.zh: 本来出自算术口诀和“数九”民俗，现多用于总结性语句。

natural: call out to one's pals

meaning.en: To gather friends together, often for fun.
meaning.zh: 招呼朋友们聚在一起（多为玩乐）。

examples.zh: 周末他喜欢呼朋唤友，去野外烧烤。
examples.en: On weekends he likes to round up his friends for a barbecue outdoors.

examples.zh: 她一高兴就呼朋唤友，家里总是热热闹闹。
examples.en: Whenever she's happy she calls her friends together, and the house is always lively.

usage.en: Neutral or slightly teasing; can imply fondness for socialising. Also 呼朋引伴.
usage.zh: 中性或略带调侃，也说“呼朋引伴”。

natural: heart drunk and spirit enchanted

meaning.en: So captivated by something beautiful that one is entranced.
meaning.zh: 对美好事物深深陶醉，神魂迷恋。

examples.zh: 听着悠扬的琴声，大家都心醉神迷。
examples.en: Listening to the melodious music, everyone was entranced.

examples.zh: 山顶的日出让游客们心醉神迷。
examples.en: The sunrise at the summit enraptured the tourists.

usage.en: Positive, literary. Used of music, scenery, beauty and love. Predicate or complement.
usage.zh: 褒义、书面色彩，多用于音乐、景色、美人等。

pinyin: fān shǒu wéi yún, fù shǒu wéi yǔ
literal: turn up · hand · make · clouds · turn over · hand · make · rain
natural: one hand turns up clouds and the other brings rain

meaning.en: Fickle and manipulative; or able to control events and manipulate people at will.
meaning.zh: 形容反复无常、玩弄手段，也形容能随意操纵局势。

examples.zh: 他翻手为云，覆手为雨，没人知道他下一步想干什么。
examples.en: He turns clouds to rain at will, and nobody knows what he'll do next.

examples.zh: 那个财团翻手为云，覆手为雨，左右着整个市场。
examples.en: That consortium manipulates events at will and sways the whole market.

examples.zh: 世态炎凉，人情冷暖，不过是翻手为云覆手为雨。
examples.en: The fickleness of human relations is just the work of a turning hand.

story.en: Du Fu's poem 'Song of Poor Friendship' laments how friends turn: 'Turning the hand up makes clouds, turning it down makes rain; so many fickle people, why count them?' (翻手作云覆手雨，纷纷轻薄何须数).
story.zh: 杜甫《贫交行》：“翻手作云覆手雨，纷纷轻薄何须数。”

usage.en: Usually derogatory, for manipulative or fickle people; sometimes also used neutrally for great power. Also used as 翻云覆雨.
usage.zh: 多含贬义，指反复无常、手段多变，也可中性指权力极大。

natural: promote on the surface, demote in reality

meaning.en: A promotion in name that actually strips away real power.
meaning.zh: 表面上提升职位，实际上削减了实权。

examples.zh: 他被任命为顾问，实际上是明升暗降。
examples.en: He was appointed adviser, which was in fact a promotion in name only.

examples.zh: 别被头衔迷惑，这一次调动明升暗降。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by the title; this transfer is a demotion in disguise.

usage.en: Used in office-politics contexts; the perspective is the person being sidelined. Predicate.
usage.zh: 多见于职场权力斗争，作谓语。

literal: sit · on the spot · divide · loot
natural: sit down and divide the loot

meaning.en: To split stolen goods among the gang; the leader or fence takes a share without taking part in the crime.
meaning.zh: 盗贼在窝点瓜分赃物；也指不动手而分取赃物。

equivalents: take a cut of the loot

examples.zh: 警方破获了一个坐地分赃的盗窃团伙。
examples.en: The police have broken up a gang that split up its stolen loot.

examples.zh: 他负责销赃，是个坐地分赃的角色。
examples.en: He handles disposal of stolen goods; he's the sort who takes a cut without lifting a finger.

usage.en: Negative; common in crime reporting and fiction. Also used figuratively for taking undeserved profit.
usage.zh: 贬义，多见于犯罪报道和小说，也比喻坐享不义之财。

natural: poverty shrinks one's ambition

meaning.en: Poverty wears down one's ambitions and self-respect.
meaning.zh: 人一旦穷了，志气就低了，容易向人低头。

examples.zh: 人穷志短，他为了一口饭竟向仇人低了头。
examples.en: Poverty crushes the spirit, and for a meal he even bowed to his enemy.

examples.zh: 俗话说人穷志短，马瘦毛长。
examples.en: As the saying goes, poverty shrinks ambition, like a lean horse has long hair.

usage.en: A sigh or explanation rather than a moral; can be countered with 穷且益坚 ('poor yet strong'). Often paired with 马瘦毛长.
usage.zh: 多作感叹或解释，不是劝诫；反驳常说“穷且益坚”。常与“马瘦毛长”连用。

natural: mix up black and white

meaning.en: To deliberately blur right and wrong, or truth and falsehood.
meaning.zh: 故意把是非、对错弄混。

examples.zh: 有些自媒体混淆黑白，误导公众。
examples.en: Some self-media confuse right and wrong and mislead the public.

examples.zh: 他在法庭上混淆黑白，企图开脱罪责。
examples.en: In court he blurred the truth, trying to escape responsibility.

examples.zh: 不能让谣言混淆黑白。
examples.en: We can't let rumours muddy the truth.

usage.en: Negative; 淆 is read xiáo ('confuse'), not yáo. Often interchangeable with 颠倒黑白, but 混淆 emphasises blurring while 颠倒 emphasises reversing.
usage.zh: 贬义；“淆”读xiáo。与“颠倒黑白”近似，但“混淆”重在弄混，“颠倒”重在倒置。

natural: body and mind both worn out

meaning.en: Utterly drained in body and spirit.
meaning.zh: 身体和精神都极度疲惫。

examples.zh: 长期加班让他身心交瘁。
examples.en: Constant overtime has left him exhausted in body and mind.

examples.zh: 照顾病人半年，她已经身心交瘁。
examples.en: After half a year caring for the patient, she is drained in body and mind.

usage.en: A slightly stronger, more formal version of 心力交瘁. Predicate.
usage.zh: 比“心力交瘁”更强调身体和精神两方面，较正式，作谓语。
